title: Charset-less text/html or text/plain Content-Type
description: The response declares text/html or text/plain without a charset parameter, so the browser has to fall back to a legacy default or to content sniffing when it decodes the page. The same bytes can then be read with a different character mapping than the server intended, which enables encoding-based script smuggling and mis-rendered content.
remediation: Immediate: declare `charset=utf-8` on every `text/html` and `text/plain` response and make sure the bytes are actually encoded that way, since a declared charset that disagrees with the payload produces mojibake rather than safety. Durable: set the `Content-Type` once in the framework or the reverse proxy instead of per handler, and keep any `<meta charset>` declaration identical to the header so the two cannot disagree. Trade-off: legacy clients that relied on automatic encoding detection now have to honour the declared encoding, which is the intended behaviour but can surface previously hidden encoding bugs.
limitation: Media-type scoped: only text/html and text/plain need a charset declaration here. application/json (RFC 8259), application/javascript (RFC 9239) and text/css are defined as UTF-8, binary types take no charset parameter, and a wholly missing Content-Type is reported by DPK-DAST-074.
